status: Test-only public API characterization candidate; no SDK compilation or WK execution.

minimum.SDK: Must contain public WKWebExtension APIs introduced with iOS18.4; runtime availability guard is not a substitute for SDK declarations.
minimum.oldOS: Explicit XCTSkip with UNSUPPORTED_PUBLIC_API; must never be counted as resource-compatibility acceptance.

APIShape.fact: Official Swift async throwing resourceBaseURL initializer, no guessed underscored/refined call.
Exact optional delegate completion-handler signature is public; async alternative is not required by this callback implementation.
Public load/unload with checked errors; no testing-mode switch or private API.
Grant only webRequest/nativeMessaging and the two owned loopback URL host scopes, not all URLs. Permission bypass method explicitly returns false.
Private-data access is restricted to the new empty, nonpersistent test data store; not existing Safari/App data or a production permission decision.
Tab returns the exact probe WKWebView whose configuration references the same controller.
Await actual background-load completion plus exact extension native-ready receipt before page navigation.
The engine allocates an additional background WKWebView. This is an explicit additional WebKit runtime context, not a single-page cost claim.
Feature-disabled implementation can return nil/unsupported. Public source availability is not proof a particular host/OS enables the feature.

lifecycle: Write only a unique temporary owned extension fixture off main; initialize through public API.
Bind one nonpersistent data store to the probe page and controller configuration; create matching window/tab adapters.
Load context and real background; validate controller identity, context identity, application id and random nonce on every native message.
Register observers before real ready ACK, then load owned loopback parent.
Record actual before/redirect/completed/error packets, request/frame ids, browser timestamp, native arrival ordinal and optional cache flag. Do not use parent Resource Timing as event proof.

Hold one real cancel-route native reply; seal event admission; await actual owned AbortController evaluation; issue stop ACK. Background really removes observers and sends stopped through nativeMessaging; test waits that receipt.
Checked public unload must yield isLoaded false. Reply pending native callback on failure, detach own handlers even when unload throws. Fixture peer stops and drains its own accepted TCP connections.

fixtures.originB: localhost same owned listener/port, distinct origin
fixtures.cache: Two force-cache fetches; accept one or two actual peer requests and record extension event count. No assumed cached-event parity.
fixtures.redirect: Actual HTTP302 from A to B and real extension redirect event required.
fixtures.frame: Require cross-origin child navigation frame and nested fetch frame identity; parent timing must not claim nested child/worker entries.

explicitLimits: No Apple SDK/compiler/WK/HTTP/extension result has executed locally.
This test does not implement sourceRegex or generalWebPolicy.resource; it characterizes the public event path only.
Additional extension background WK context/memory and OS18.4 floor require an explicit future production decision; iOS17 remains unsupported by this route.
No proof of Android resource timing/first-match parity, absence of late events, full resource-body access or all cached/worker/service-worker combinations.
CSP/DNR-blocked resources, source-revision replacement during background activation, external Swift Task cancellation during setup, process termination and all MIME/request classes remain uncovered.

Explicit observer seal/stop/unload is tested; no claim public unload waits for every WebContent process to die or rolls back already sent HTTP. Peer counts mean accepted requests, not successful response commits.
ATS/local-network permission, framework feature availability and real callback delivery must be measured in the future host. Missing API/OS/load/permission cannot become a fake pass.
Owned WKScriptMessage page completion is only fixture coordination. Only exact extension delegate receipts count as observer proof.
